raw_response:
I'm 72 this year, and these 9 mu have been my life for 50 years. My legs aren't what they used to be, and with only three of us at home — my wife and me, plus our son who works at the factory in town and only comes back for the busy seasons — I have to watch every yuan. We don't have much cash lying around, and I'm too old to take big risks.

**The 7 mu of wheat and maize:** I'll do what I've always done. Wheat goes in around October 10th, same time as everyone in the village. I use Jinmai 47 — saved some seed from last year, bought the rest from Old Wang down the road. About 15 jin per mu, costs me roughly 30 yuan. For fertilizer, I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting — that's about 40 kg. Then at jointing in March, if the wheat looks a bit yellow, I'll topdress with another 10 kg of urea. I can't afford more than that. Last year I got about 380 kg per mu, and I'm hoping for the same if the weather holds. I irrigate three times — once after planting if it's dry, once at green-up, and once at grain filling. The pump electricity isn't cheap, but without water you get nothing around here.

For maize, it's always a rush after wheat harvest in mid-June. I cut the wheat, and within two days the maize seed is in the ground. No time for plowing — I plant right into the stubble. I use about 3 jin of hybrid seed per mu, costs about 25 yuan. One bag of compound fertilizer at planting, around 12 kg of nitrogen per mu. Maybe irrigate twice if July gets hot and dry. Last year maize gave me 420 kg per mu, but I'll hope for 400 to be safe.

**The 2 mu of cotton:** I've kept this cotton plot for years. Planted in late April, and we're picking through September and October. I use less fertilizer on cotton — about 30 kg of compound fertilizer per mu, one application. Irrigate twice, maybe three times. Cotton gives steady money, but the picking is back-breaking work. My wife handles most of it. I expect about 250 kg of seed cotton per mu.

**Labor and costs:** Most of the work is just us old folks. For wheat harvest and maize planting, we hire a couple days of help — maybe 5 days total for the whole year. Our son helps about 10 days during the peak times. I figure seed, fertilizer, pesticide, irrigation electricity, and hired labor will run me about 2,800 yuan total this year. That's all I can spend. I'd rather put down a bit more fertilizer than risk a bad yield — a poor harvest hurts more than saving a few yuan on inputs.
